draft.title: Parts of a business plan
card: A business plan is split into parts. Each part has its own goals and actions, and together they work towards the business's overall goals.
how the business will find and keep customers. It covers the product, price, promotion and place.
how the business will make its product or deliver its service. It covers things like suppliers, equipment and production methods.
Finance covers the money needed, expected sales and costs, and cash flow. Human resources covers how staff are hired, trained and managed.
draft.remember: Each part of a plan answers its own question, with its own goals and actions.

a.q: Which part of a business plan would set out how many staff to hire and how to train them?
a.why: Human resources covers how staff are hired, trained and managed. Operations is the most tempting wrong answer, but it covers how the product is made or the service is delivered, not how staff are hired and trained.
a.clue: Which part is about the people who work for the business?

b.q: Mia plans to open a bakery in Dubbo. She is working out which flour supplier to use and what ovens to buy. Which part of her plan is this?
b.why: Choosing suppliers and equipment is about how the bakery will make its product, so it belongs in operations. Finance is tempting because ovens cost money, but finance covers money needed, sales, costs and cash flow, not how the product is made.
b.clue: Which part covers how the product is made?
